title: Roy Rogers
paragraphs: A family Western adventure series starring Roy Rogers, often joined by Dale Evans and familiar supporting characters in stories mixing action, humor, music, and frontier justice.
Family-oriented singing-cowboy Western starring Roy Rogers, frequently with Dale Evans and later Pat Brady, mixing adventure, humor, music and contemporary technology in a stylized modern West.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Mutual first run (November 21, 1944 to May 8, 1945) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], NBC run (October 5, 1946 to March 29, 1947) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Mutual transcribed Western era (1948-08 to May 13, 1951) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and NBC final run (October 5, 1951 to July 21, 1955) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|roy-rogers|Roy Rogers]] (performer), Dale Evans (performer), Art Ballinger (announcer), Art Rush (producer, performer, and production supervisor), Milton Charles (performer and music), Frank Hemingway (performer), and Pat Brady (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].
The stories often return to western song and musical performance, ranching and cattle, outlaws and criminal gangs, outlaws and banditry, frontier law and justice, and mining and gold.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Singing-cowboy radio format, Early transcribed network production, Sponsor premiums and youth marketing, and Radio/television overlap.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|wild-bill-hickok|Wild Bill Hickok]], and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]].
